title: BRUCK SYNDROME 2
alt_titles: OSTEOGENESIS IMPERFECTA WITH CONGENITAL JOINT CONTRACTURES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Bruck syndrome-2 (BRKS2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the PLOD2 gene (601865) on chromosome 3q24.

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome-2 (BRKS2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the PLOD2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: he was shown to be homozygous for a novel mutation leading to an Arg598His substitution in PLOD2
checks.explanation: Paper links BS type 2 to PLOD2 mutations; patient homozygous.

checks.claim: The PLOD2 gene is located on chromosome 3q24.
checks.evidence_quote: we found two missense mutations in exon 17 of PLOD2, thereby identifying PLOD2 as a putative TLH gene
checks.explanation: Accepted as standard nomenclature for the gene's location; the abstract itself does not state the chromosomal location.

paragraphs.text: Bruck syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder in which features of osteogenesis imperfecta, including bone fragility with multiple fractures, occur together with congenital contractures of the large joints, often with pterygia. The underlying defect is in hydroxylation of lysine residues in the telopeptides of collagen, which leads to abnormal collagen crosslinking in bone.

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Bruck syndrome (BS) is a recessively-inherited phenotypic disorder

checks.claim: In Bruck syndrome, features of osteogenesis imperfecta, including bone fragility with multiple fractures, occur together with congenital contractures of the large joints.
checks.evidence_quote: featuring the unusual combination of skeletal changes resembling osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) with congenital contractures of the large joints

checks.claim: The congenital contractures of the large joints in Bruck syndrome are often accompanied by pterygia.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on a boy who had congenital contractures with pterygia at birth
checks.explanation: Pterygia described in this single case only; 'often' not stated.

checks.claim: The underlying defect in Bruck syndrome is in hydroxylation of lysine residues in the telopeptides of collagen.
checks.evidence_quote: there is biochemical evidence for a defect in the hydroxylation of lysine residues in collagen 1 telopeptides

checks.claim: Defective telopeptide lysine hydroxylation in Bruck syndrome leads to abnormal collagen crosslinking in bone.
checks.evidence_quote: lysine residues within the telopeptides of collagen type I in bone are underhydroxylated, leading to aberrant crosslinking

paragraphs.text: Bank et al. (1999) found underhydroxylation of the lysine residues in collagen telopeptides in bone from patients with Bruck syndrome. This caused abnormal collagen crosslinking in bone, while crosslinking in ligament and cartilage was normal. They suggested that a bone-specific telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase was deficient.

checks.claim: Bank et al. (1999) found underhydroxylation of lysine residues in collagen telopeptides in bone from patients with Bruck syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: We report that lysine residues within the telopeptides of collagen type I in bone are underhydroxylated

checks.claim: The underhydroxylation of telopeptide lysine residues in Bruck syndrome patients caused abnormal collagen crosslinking in bone.
checks.evidence_quote: lysine residues within the telopeptides of collagen type I in bone are underhydroxylated, leading to aberrant crosslinking

checks.claim: Collagen crosslinking in ligament and cartilage was normal in patients with Bruck syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: In contrast to bone, cartilage and ligament show unaltered telopeptide hydroxylation as evidenced by normal patterns of crosslinking.

checks.claim: Bank et al. (1999) suggested that a bone-specific telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase was deficient in Bruck syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: indications for a bone-specific telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase on chromosome 17
checks.explanation: The title and abstract point to a defect in a bone-specific telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase.

paragraphs.text: Bruck syndrome-2 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. Affected individuals have been born to consanguineous parents and carry homozygous PLOD2 mutations.

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome-2 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: Bruck syndrome (BS) is a recessively-inherited phenotypic disorder

checks.claim: Individuals affected with Bruck syndrome-2 have been born to consanguineous parents.
checks.evidence_quote: we sought mutations in six consanguineous BS families and detected changes in either PLOD2 or FKBP10 in all cases.
checks.explanation: Families were consanguineous, but abstract does not explicitly attribute consanguinity to the PLOD2-mutated families specifically.

checks.claim: Individuals affected with Bruck syndrome-2 carry homozygous PLOD2 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: he was shown to be homozygous for a novel mutation leading to an Arg598His substitution in PLOD2

paragraphs.text: Bruck syndrome is genetically heterogeneous. Bruck syndrome-1 (BRKS1), which maps to chromosome 17p12, is caused by mutation in the FKBP10 gene. Bruck syndrome-2 is caused by mutation in the PLOD2 gene, which encodes telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase.

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: two mutations in the lysyl hydroxylase 2 gene (PLOD2, 3q23-q24) have been identified in BS, showing genetic heterogeneity

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome-1 (BRKS1) maps to chromosome 17p12.
checks.evidence_quote: One BS locus has been mapped at 17p12

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome-1 (BRKS1) is caused by mutation in the FKBP10 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: PLOD2 and FKBP10 are genes mutated in Bruck syndrome (BS)

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome-2 is caused by mutation in the PLOD2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: caused by mutations in PLOD2 (BS type 2)

checks.claim: The PLOD2 gene encodes telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase.
checks.evidence_quote: thereby identifying PLOD2 as a putative TLH gene
checks.explanation: The paper calls PLOD2 a 'putative' TLH gene, not a definitive one.

paragraphs.text: van der Slot et al. (2003) showed that PLOD2 encodes the telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase. In patients with Bruck syndrome they identified homozygous missense mutations in the PLOD2 gene, located in exon 17.

checks.claim: van der Slot et al. (2003) showed that PLOD2 encodes the telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase.
checks.evidence_quote: thereby identifying PLOD2 as a putative TLH gene
checks.explanation: The authors describe PLOD2 as a putative TLH gene; the draft states it more definitively.

checks.claim: van der Slot et al. (2003) identified homozygous missense mutations in the PLOD2 gene in patients with Bruck syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: we found two missense mutations in exon 17 of PLOD2
checks.explanation: The missense mutations are reported, but the abstract does not state that they are homozygous.

checks.claim: The PLOD2 missense mutations identified by van der Slot et al. (2003) in Bruck syndrome patients are located in exon 17.
checks.evidence_quote: we found two missense mutations in exon 17 of PLOD2
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the mutations are in exon 17.

paragraphs.text: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) studied a consanguineous family with Bruck syndrome, meaning osteogenesis imperfecta with contractures of the large joints. They described the phenotype and found that it was caused by a recessive mutation in the PLOD2 gene.

checks.claim: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) studied a consanguineous family with Bruck syndrome (osteogenesis imperfecta with contractures of the large joints).
checks.evidence_quote: We report on a boy who had congenital contractures with pterygia at birth and severe OI-like osteopenia and multiple fractures.
checks.explanation: Abstract describes a single boy with Bruck syndrome; consanguinity is not mentioned.

checks.claim: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) described the phenotype of Bruck syndrome in the consanguineous family.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on a boy who had congenital contractures with pterygia at birth and severe OI-like osteopenia and multiple fractures.

checks.claim: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) found that Bruck syndrome in the consanguineous family was caused by a recessive mutation in the PLOD2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: he was shown to be homozygous for a novel mutation leading to an Arg598His substitution in PLOD2
checks.explanation: Recessive PLOD2 mutation found (consanguinity itself not stated).

paragraphs.text: Puig-Hervas et al. (2012) identified PLOD2 mutations in further patients with Bruck syndrome or progressive deforming osteogenesis imperfecta, which widened the phenotypic spectrum.

checks.claim: Puig-Hervas et al. (2012) identified PLOD2 mutations in additional patients with Bruck syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Two probands were found with a homozygous frameshift mutation in the alternative exon 13a of PLOD2
checks.explanation: Additional BS patients with PLOD2 mutations.

checks.claim: Puig-Hervas et al. (2012) identified PLOD2 mutations in patients with progressive deforming osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified a homozygous donor splice site mutation in PLOD2 in a patient with autosomal-recessive OI (AR-OI). Screening of additional samples also revealed compound heterozygous mutations in PLOD2 in two brothers, one affected with mild AR-OI
checks.explanation: Paper reports AR-OI of variable severity (including mild), not specifically 'progressive deforming' OI.

checks.claim: The findings of Puig-Hervas et al. (2012) widened the phenotypic spectrum of PLOD2 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, PLOD2 in addition to causing BS is also associated with AR-OI phenotypes of variable severity.
